evidence.excerpt: Twelve steel electrical cabinets installed in four unheated substations in Vojvodina were instrumented with internal and external temperature–humidity loggers over a 14-month period spanning two winters. Internal relative humidity exceeded 85 % for more than 480 hours per year in cabinets without anti-condensation heaters, with the longest continuous exceedance episode lasting 61 hours. A lumped-parameter hygrothermal model driven by measured exterior boundary conditions reproduced the measured internal humidity with a root-mean-square error of 3.2 percentage points. Model calibration identified the dominant vapour pathway as the cable entry glands rather than the door gasket, accounting for approximately 68 % of total vapour ingress. Anti-condensation heater power requirements derived from the model range from 6 W to 22 W depending on cabinet volume. Recommendations for gland specification and heater sizing are given.
